screening.base: Reuse approved proportion-study validation-only tuning rows at the saved per-maze p*. Pilot default identity permits reuse.
screening.selection: Per maze and axis: mean over registered points within seed, then mean over five validation seeds; maximize; candidates within 1e-12 of maximum tie, base wins ties, otherwise earlier registered setting.

test.derivation: Recompute saved selection from complete screening and frozen validation-only base rows. Run only selected non-base axes and mazes; base selections cause no allocations.

arms: S at p* from proportion test
acs2 and acs2er from pair baseline
references.policy: Reuse twenty-seed verified references without rerunning them. The six default pilot trajectories are identity controls, not new reference estimates.

forecast.estimate_rule: Seed42 allocation CPUTimeRAW; three-block pilots conservatively proxy validation-only screening. Worst selected B schedule and all three C arms per maze, both axes tested everywhere.
forecast.screening_group_rule: Sort cells by hard limit and pilot allocation cost, then choose contiguous groups of four to eight five-seed cells minimizing total hard reservations; ties use fewer arrays, then earlier boundaries. No success values enter grouping.
forecast.limit_rule: max(3, ceil((2 * body wall seconds + 60) / 60)) minutes, common maximum within each screening array; one twenty-seed array per test arm.
forecast.limitation: One seed measures cost, not seed variability or scientific benefit. Every attempt and outstanding reservation remains charged.

analysis.primary: Average all registered points equally within seed, then mean and SE across twenty seeds.
analysis.final: Use last registered point per seed, then mean and SE across twenty seeds.

aliases.S: shortened HER at saved p* with constant independent replay
aliases.E: episodic ER with constant independent replay

analysis.threshold_arithmetic: For S_X only: exact exhaustive integer counts and Fraction means; inclusive >= both registered baseline final means; first nominal point, no interpolation, null if unreached.
analysis.screening_table: Mean and SE of five validation checkpoint-mean seed scores for every maze and setting, including reused base; no screening test-block access.
diagnostics: realized updates / interactions for every checkpoint interval from cumulative differences
requested pass share, realized copy share, fallbacks, trivial copies, post-end copies, rewarded copies, wall copies
first-action value minus return for all, successful and failed test pairs
memory lower bounds and peak RSS
objective calls by scoring, selection and provenance
allocated CPUTimeRAW, process user+system CPU and cost by pilot, screening, test and reused historical purpose
analysis.diagnostic_aggregation: Within each row use appropriate route denominators; checkpoint_mean averages equally within seed; final_point uses only last row; then mean/SE over seeds. Empty groups stay null with counts.
analysis.interpretation: B deliberately changes update volume. Same settings equalize the rule and prescribed volume between S_X and E_X; realized totals may differ with episode overshoot and episode-end switch rounding. C compares full passes against independent sampling; random-pass control isolates within-pass order.
limitations: Length-proportional episode selection followed by whole passes does not preserve uniform transition replay frequencies. For original full passes, expected exposure per transition grows with episode length; counterfactual prefixes add goal-dependent weighting.
One-goal passes change copy weighting: p is per pass, realized per-update share need not equal p. Report pass and draw counts separately.
Backward and random control share pass samples and goals conditional on identical stores and sampler state; learned policies and subsequent real trajectories can diverge.
Intervals condition on selected settings and do not include selection uncertainty. Finite training horizons do not establish convergence.
analysis.post_hoc: Every other comparison, including every success comparison against ACS2, is labelled post hoc.

identity_checks.base: Every default seed42 row reproduces proportion-study selected-p test learning, knowledge and all three blocks in binary64 bits. STOP on mismatch.
identity_checks.screening: Seed42 validation and shared learning fields reproduce the full-block pilot.
identity_checks.test: Seed42 all blocks reproduce pilot; seeds42--46 reproduce screening on validation and every learning/knowledge field for S_X.
identity_checks.exclusions: Only grid_identity.OMIT: source/hardware/time provenance and arm annotation.

execution.dispatch: One-shot dispatcher, one registered 20--40-job array per invocation; at most two active streams and forty running jobs. No dependent queue of future arrays.
execution.admission: Re-derive each manifest from exact approved bytes and recomputed saved selection before every sbatch; grant and sbatch --test-only; pilot + used + reserved + new hard limits within approved cap.
execution.accounting: One scope over every root; zero pilot offset; all allocations and failed attempts included exactly once; hard reservations include whole array maxima.
execution.guards: Pinned clean source, static binary and immutable operations; node guards; shared STOP on real failure; diagnosed recovery and bitwise partial-prefix equality before retry acceptance.

authorization: Stage1 only: sixty seed42 pilot allocations within twelve CPU-hours including reservations. Screening and test require explicit approval of this plan and a cumulative CPU-hour limit; stop after registration.
